ai.description: This snake reaches 40–50 cm. It is reddish-brown with a series of dark, light-centered vertebral spots and a distinctive V-shaped mark on the head. It possesses enlarged, blade-like rear teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Travancore Kukri Snake is best distinguished by its distinct, dark-edged, reddish-brown vertebral stripe that runs the entire length of its body.
ai.habitat: The Travancore Kukri Snake inhabits the moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Travancore Kukri snake is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice open reptile eggs, which form a significant part of its diet.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon travancoricus* is oviparous, typically laying small clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months (April to August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon travancoricus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 600 and 1,500 meters.
